text:
Zoe M.: heads up, staging linkcheck failed after the content import; looks like frontmatter title normalization and an EOL quirk removed an anchor.

BuildBot: linkcheck step failed in build #1402: https://ci.redwood/1402 :warning:

Zoe M.: excerpt from logs:
```
WARN Broken fragment: /how-to/ops-runbook.md#on-call-checklist -> fragment not found
WARN Missing anchor: generated anchor for 'On‑call checklist' differs (expected '#on-call-checklist', got '#on-call-checklist-1')
WARN Heading not generated: heading after fenced code block suppressed -> /reference/formatting.md#note-style
```

Ken H.: I ran a quick scan: the frontmatter `title:` in several migrated files had trailing spaces or non-breaking spaces which Docusaurus slugifier handled differently, and one file had a CRLF -> LF conversion issue so the parser didn't emit the heading anchor after a fenced block.

Priya S.: Grep results: `rg "#on-call-checklist" docs/ --hidden` -> 4 hits in examples and one internal README. The canonical page now has the generated suffix `#on-call-checklist-1` because another page uses the same title and the slugifier de-duplicated.

Luis A.: For the suppressed heading after a code fence, I reproduced locally: when a fenced block isn't followed by a blank line, the MDX AST attaches the heading to the code block and the heading id isn't emitted. Quick fix is insert a blank line between the fence and the heading.

Zoe M.: Proposed fixes: 1) add explicit short ids on canonical headings that must keep stable anchors (eg `## On-call checklist {#on-call-checklist}`) 2) update the 4 broken refs to point to the canonical id 3) fix the code-fence spacing in formatting.md 4) add a tiny CI check that validates changed-file fragments and warns on trailing non-breaking spaces in frontmatter.

Priya S.: I'm happy to open a small PR that does the three ref updates and adds the explicit id. I'll also run `pnpm docs:build && pnpm docs:linkcheck` locally.

Ken H.: I'll handle the code-fence spacing fix and add a one-line unit in `tests/` that scans for `\n```.*\n###` patterns (i.e., fence immediately followed by heading) and fails the test.

BuildBot: Suggested PR checklist:
- [ ] Add explicit `{#on-call-checklist}` id on canonical page `/how-to/ops-runbook.md`
- [ ] Update 4 internal refs in examples/ and README to point at `#on-call-checklist`
- [ ] Fix blank-line-after-fence in `/reference/formatting.md` so heading IDs are emitted
- [ ] Add `tests/check_changed_fragments.sh` and `tests/check_frontmatter_nbsp.sh`
- [ ] Run `pnpm docs:build && pnpm docs:linkcheck` locally and CI will run the rest

Zoe M.: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1187 - includes explicit id, three ref updates, and a small test harness for changed fragments. Ken pushed the fence spacing fix to the same branch.

BuildBot: PR 1187 - linkcheck queued in CI.

Priya S.: I ran `pnpm docs:linkcheck` locally; fixed a stray example that referenced the old suffixed anchor. All good locally.

BuildBot: CI for PR 1187 - linkcheck passed :white_check_mark: minor linter warning about frontmatter whitespace fixed automatically.

Luis A.: Merged. Staging linkcheck is green and the runbook anchor resolves to `#on-call-checklist`. I also added a one-liner in `docs/MIGRATION.md` about frontmatter trailing whitespace causing slug differences.

Zoe M.: Thanks everyone. Filing an infra ticket to add the changed-file fragment check as a pre-commit hook so we catch this earlier. Closing thread. :tada:
